drafts.title: I calculated actual cost-per-line-of-code across 12 AI coding assistants. Copilot Individual beats most 'premium' tools.
drafts.text:
Ran the actual math on AI coding tool costs using the metric that actually matters: cost per accepted line of code.

The formula: (monthly seat cost) / (active hours × suggestions/hr × acceptance rate × lines/accepted suggestion)

Key findings after running it across Cursor, Copilot, Claude Code, Windsurf, Cody, Tabnine, JetBrains AI, and Continue:

- GitHub Copilot Individual ($10/seat) has the best cost-per-line for most teams (~$0.22)
- Cursor Pro ($20/seat) comes in at $0.48/line — not bad, but not the deal it looks like
- Cursor Business ($40/seat) is $0.96/line — identical model quality to Pro, you're paying for admin features
- Enterprise tiers across every tool are priced for compliance, not code quality
- Continue (OSS) + Claude Haiku API is the cheapest at ~$0.16/line if you can self-host

The biggest hidden variable: acceptance rate drift. Teams new to a tool start at 15-20% acceptance and climb to 35-45% over 6 months. Your month-1 cost model overstates the long-term cost significantly.

I built a calculator to run this for your specific team size, tool, and usage pattern:
https://tinytools-smoky.vercel.app/ai-coding-assistant-cost-calc/blog/i-calculated-ai-coding-assistant-cost-per-line-of-code-2026/

Happy to share the raw numbers/assumptions if anyone wants to poke holes in the methodology.

I just realized: almost nobody in engineering leadership knows what their AI coding tools actually cost per accepted line of code. They know the seat price. That's not the same thing.

I ran the math across 12 tools — Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Windsurf, Cody, and others. The most expensive option per accepted line isn't the most expensive per seat. The cheapest isn't always the best value.

The counterintuitive finding: GitHub Copilot Individual at $10/seat beats most "premium" tools on cost-per-line, partly because its flat completion model keeps acceptance rates stable.

For a 10-person team, the difference between the right and wrong AI coding stack choice is $25,000–$40,000 per year in sunk cost — for statistically equivalent productivity gains.

Built a calculator that compares AI coding assistant costs using cost-per-accepted-line-of-code rather than per-seat price, because per-seat is a misleading metric.

The formula: (monthly cost) / (active hours × suggestions/hr × acceptance rate × avg lines per accepted suggestion)

Covers Cursor, GitHub Copilot (all tiers), Claude Code, Windsurf, Cody, Tabnine, JetBrains AI, Continue, Augment, and Replit Agent. You can enter your team's actual acceptance rate if you have it, or use tool-specific estimates from developer productivity surveys.

Key finding from running the numbers: Copilot Individual ($10/seat) outperforms most "premium" tools on cost-per-line. Cursor Business ($40/seat) is identical model quality to Cursor Pro ($20/seat) — you're paying for SSO and audit logs. Claude Code is expensive per-line but isn't an inline completion tool — compare it against agentic task completion.
